name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 2, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:01
p.m., on February 2, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 30, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

CALL TO ORDER

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  February 2, 2009
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess to closed session. The City
  Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed item CS1 in Closed
  Session and provided direction to the City’s negotiators. Items CS2 and CS3 will be
  considered after the open session portion of the meeting.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize 2008 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Ury presented plaques to (1) Library Page, Michael Bailey, City of Mission Viejo
  Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Brad Blakely, Orange County Sheriff’s Department
  Employee of the Year; and (3) Fire Captain Kelly Zimmerman, Orange County Fire
  Authority Employee of the Year.

P2.  Certificate of Appreciation to the Mission Viejo Elks Lodge #2444

  Mayor Ury presented the Certificate of Appreciation to Mike Holohan, representing Elks
  Lodge #2444.

P3.  Presentation by Townsend Public Affairs on Reauthorization of the Safe
  Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Equity Act: A Legacy for Users
  (SAFETEA-LU) and American Recovery and Reinvestment Act.

  The City Council received the presentation from Christopher Townsend, Townsend
  Public Affairs.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  James D. Burns, President of the Timberline Homeowners Association, M.V.: stated that
  the Timberline HOA is concerned that the City Council Members are not aware of the
  issues surrounding Turf Lane Park and he asked the Council to address and settle this
  ongoing matter.
  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern that 24 Rose Parade tickets were given away as
  "freebies" including one to a member of the press and several more to VIP riders of the
  float.

City Council Minutes  2  February 2, 2009
   Margo Kutner and Hilda Baitoo, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Mission Viejo Cultural
  Arts Committee, extended sincere thanks to the City Manager, members of city staff and
  to the City Council Members for supporting art programs. They provided an overview of
  upcoming events and reminded everyone to arrive early as many programs are sold out.

  Carol Tagayun, External Affairs Director for AT&T: addressed an inaccurate blog
  posting regarding an alleged AT&T promotional offering. She stated that there is no
  such AT&T promotion and that they do not run advertisements that disparage their
  competitors.

  Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: speaking in reference to the plans to build additional tennis and
  basketball courts at the Marguerite Tennis Center, he stated that new courts are
  unnecessary and that it is time to stop supporting a small group when revenues are down.

  Jim Holmes, M.V.: representing the Board of Directors of the Friends of the Library, Mr.
  Holmes discussed the success of the January 31st Writer’s Presents program featuring
  Robert Wagner and he announced that Cloris Leachman will visit Mission Viejo in May.

  Rebecca Price, M.V.: submitted a written comment regarding the overhead power lines
  off La Barca and Marguerite. She noted that the lines have spoiled views and they
  present a health hazard.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, and 4 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  3  February 2, 2009
 5.  General Plan Amendment GPA2007-27, being a City-initiated petition to update to
  the Noise Element and re-adopt the existing Public Safety Element of the City’s
  General Plan. The Noise Element consists of goals and policies to limit exposure of
  the community to excessive noise levels. The Public Safety Element consists of goals
  and polices to mitigate identified hazards specific to Mission Viejo

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:20 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing. After hearing no
  comments from members of the public, the Mayor closed the public hearing.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Schlicht,
  to (1) adopt Resolution 09-06 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2007-27 to
  Update to the Noise Element and Re-adopt the Existing Public Safety Element of the
  City’s General Plan; and (2) adopt Negative Declaration declaring proposed General Plan
  Amendment GPA2007-27 as it pertains to the Noise Element and Public Safety Element
  will not have a significant adverse impact on the environment for the purpose of CEQA
  review.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  Twelve Month Extension of Interim Ordinance No. 08-267 Regarding A
  Moratorium On The Change Of Use For All Recreation And Open Space Land
  Within The City Pending Further Study

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:33 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing. After hearing no
  comments from members of the public, the Mayor closed the public hearing.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean,
  to adopt Ordinance 09-274 Approving a Twelve Month Extension of Interim Ordinance
  No. 08-267 Declaring and Imposing a Moratorium on the Granting of Any Requests For
  Changes to the General Plan and/or Any Specific Plans, Changes of Zone, and Any and
  All Land Use Entitlements Regardless of Type or Title, Together with All Building
  Permits or Similar Entitlements For, Upon or Applying to Any Land Designated As, or

City Council Minutes  4  February 2, 2009
   Improved As Recreational and/or Open Space Within the City of Mission Viejo During
  the Term of this Interim Ordinance, and Declaring the Urgency Thereof.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  City Attorney Bill Curley read the Ordinance title for the public record.

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

7.  Check Register dated January 9, 2009, in the amount of $700,924.69

  Council Member Schlicht asked questions about several checks listed on the register.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein announced
  that he will get back to the Council with answers to the questions, as he does not have the
  backup information readily available.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean,
  to ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 19, 2009, as
  amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  February 2, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Amendment: include in the Roll Call section, page 1, notation that the City Attorney
  arrived at 5:03 p.m.

3.  Amendment to Agreement for Building Plan Check and Inspection Services and for
  Public Works Support Services - Charles Abbott Associates, Inc.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma to
  approve the First Amendment of Agreement with Charles Abbott Associates, Inc. for
  Building Plan Check and Inspection Services and for Public Works Support Services for
  the Period from July 1, 2009 to June 30, 2011.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Residential Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to (1) certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

8.  Committee Appointments

City Council Minutes  6  February 2, 2009
   Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked why a Check Register Review Committee is necessary since
  all the Council Members have a responsibility to review the city’s expenditures.

  Barbara Anderson, M.V.: stated that the city has an opportunity for innovative solutions
  to traffic issues and she supports the idea of a Roundabout Intersections Committee.

  Mayor Ury established three committees and appointed members as follows:

  (1) Standing Economic Development Committee – Mayor Pro Tem MacLean and
  Council Member Kelley.

  (2) Standing Check Register Review Committee – Council Member Schlicht.

  (3) Ad Hoc Roundabout Intersections Committee – Council Member Schlicht.

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

10.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA but he but outlined recent direction that the SJHTCA Board gave to
  staff to engage in public outreach efforts.

11.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

12.  South Orange County Gateway Improvement Program

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley,
  to adopt Resolution 09-07 Supporting Funding for the South Orange County Gateway
  Improvement Program Through the Reauthorization of the Safe, Accountable, Flexible,
  Efficient Transportation Equity Act: A Legacy for Users (SAFETEA-LU).

City Council Minutes  7  February 2, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma to
  direct staff to continue pursuing funding opportunities for the projects listed in Exhibit B
  (page 15) of the staff report, including the use of Opticom in the Citywide Traffic Signal
  Coordination Upgrade project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to also pursue funding opportunities for
  green building, solar power, water conservation and energy efficiency.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:43 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:56
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Attorney’s Report

13.  Request for City Council Direction Regarding the City Council’s Alternate
  Statutory Responses to the Vote on Private and Public Property Land Use
  Regulation Initiative

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and requested direction from the City
  Council.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  direct staff to prepare a report on the effects of the Land Use Regulation Initiative as
  outlined in Elections Code Section 9212.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None

City Council Minutes  8  February 2, 2009
   ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

  Mayor Ury and Mayor Pro Tem MacLean discussed the recent League of California
  Cities Seminars that they attended in Sacramento.

Council Member Kelley

  Highlighted her attendance at the Jennie Finch Softball camp which was held at the
  Alicia fields. She noted that it was a beautiful day, there were 300 girls in attendance,
  and Ms. Finch complimented the city on its world class fields. Council Member Kelley
  stated that this was another example of some of the good things that happen here in
  Mission Viejo at our great facilities. She discussed her attendance at the Robert Wagner
  author series program and stated that we couldn’t have held such a grand event without
  the new and expanded Murray Center. She commended Director of Library Services
  Valerie Maginnis and the Friends of the Library for their planning and insight and stated
  that we all look forward to the event in May when Cloris Leachman is the featured
  author. Council Member Kelley congratulated the three employees of the year who were
  recognized tonight and she discussed a public speaker’s comments earlier in the evening.
  Council Member Kelley expressed her concern that this individual was dissatisfied that
  the city did not release last names and ages of the Rose Parade float volunteers. She
  wondered what residents would want to volunteer for the city if they knew that their
  names and the ages of their children might be released in a public records request.
  Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month
  of February is unity.

Council Member Ledesma

  Thanked Mayor Ury and Townsend Public Affairs for providing insight into the time and
  effort involved in shaping policies at the State level.

Council Member Schlicht

15.  Honoring Federal Holidays

City Council Minutes  9  February 2, 2009
   Motion was made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to postpone the 2nd Council Meetings in January and February when Monday is a
  Federal Holiday and to move the Community Services Commission Meetings when they
  are scheduled the same week.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Discussion of Council Rules of Order

  No action taken.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that we all have different talents. Mayor Ury and Mayor
  Pro Tem MacLean are interested in regional issues and she prefers to be involved in local
  matters.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury announced that he had a delightful time at the Elks Police Officer
  Recognition dinner and he enjoyed the intergenerational conversations. He asked Mayor
  Pro Tem MacLean and Council Member Kelley if they can schedule a meeting of the
  new Economic Development Committee in the near future to begin working on the
  committee's charter. He asked council Member Schlicht if she would like to meet with
  members of staff to discuss process and who she would like to meet with first. Council
  Member Schlicht replied that she will take care of that on a personal level. Finally,
  Mayor Ury asked staff to make sure that Council Member Schlicht gets copies of the
  Master Plan of Arterial Highways, the Recreation Master Plan, CAFR's for the last 3
  years, housing element information and copies of the Mejia lawsuit, final ruling on the
  lawsuit, and information on any zoning changes to preclude further lawsuits of the same
  nature.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 9:53 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess to Closed Session. The City
  Council reconvened at 11:15 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  10  February 2, 2009
   City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed
  Session.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 11:17 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City
  Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 16, 2009,
  at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 16, 2009

City Council Minutes  11  February 2, 2009
